newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ASX to launch block trading facility.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ASX to launch block trading facility.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) said on Thursday it planned to introduce a new trading facility to provide greater flexibility for institutional investors and large "block" traders.
The facility, designed to boost market liqudity, would involve a weighted price auction to be held 15 minutes after the close of trade each day.
The ASX said the rapid growth of global institutional investment had led to pressure for trading methods that minimised the market impact of large orders.
A number of proprietary trading systems had been developed overseas to meet "block" trading needs, the ASX said.
These operated as anonymous markets where the details of buying and selling orders were not disclosed, it said.

"The problem is that these trading systems tend to draw liquidity away from the central market and thus may fragment the market. Overall liqudity suffers," ASX managing director Richard Humphry said in a statement.
Under the new system, which will operate as part of the Stock Exchange Automated Trading System (SEATS), a weighted price auction would be held each day 4.15 p.m.
This would allow brokers to channel competing bids and offers into the market during a 15-minute period after the normal close of trade, the ASX said.
All overlapping bids and offers for a security at 4.15 p.m. would be executed using a single weighted average price.
This initial facility, intended to be introduced in early 1997, would retain current levels of order disclosure.
The exchange said it was also examining designs for an anonymous market that would allow parcels of shares to be bought and sold for a known fixed price at a fixed time.
However it said this would require changes to ASX systems, as well as regulatory approval, and was unlikely to be available before mid-1997.
